steps.do: In the left sidebar, under the Integrations and preview group (the page carries a Preview badge), click Plans. This is Aria's goal-planner. The flagship demo: one sentence decomposes into a whole governance scaffold — a faithfulness judge, an eval dataset, and a human-review queue — in a single plan.
steps.see: The Aria Plans page with a Goal text box, an Autonomy dropdown, and a Decompose goal button.

steps.where: Integrations and preview › Plans › New goal
steps.do: Type Aria's one-line intent into the Goal box, using the canonical wording verbatim. The three literal needles — judge, eval dataset, and review queue — are what make the default planner propose all three creates. Then set the Autonomy dropdown to Stop before each change (the ask_each level) so Aria pauses on every step.
fill: Stand up our governance starter kit: a judge for answer faithfulness, an eval dataset to score against, and a review queue for human checks. (canonical intent — copy from intent.md)
Stop before each change (= ask_each)
steps.see: The button shows Decomposing…, then Aria opens the new plan's detail page. The breadcrumb reads Plans › PLAN-… and the status badge says DRAFT.

steps.do: Read the Plan steps list and confirm Aria found all four steps. Three are the artifacts you want; the fourth (review_queue.add_items) is proposed only because it shares the "review queue" domain — you will skip it later (no traces yet). Compare against expected-plan.json.
steps.see: A four-row Plan steps list (judge.create, review_queue.create, eval_dataset.create, review_queue.add_items) in registry order, each with a PENDING badge.

steps.do: Approve the plan shape (you are signing off on which steps run, not running them yet). Click Approve plan in the top-right of the plan header.
steps.see: The status badge flips from DRAFT to APPROVED, and an Execute button appears.

steps.do: Start running the plan. Click Execute. Aria reaches the first step, judge.create, but the planner could not know the judge's name or instructions, so it pauses on a violet Aria needs information form with a field per capability input (name and instructions are required) and two buttons, Continue plan and Skip step.
steps.see: The judge.create row shows WAITING INPUT and an Aria needs information form is open above the step list.

steps.where: Integrations and preview › Plans › PLAN-… (input form)
steps.do: Fill the judge form from answer-faithfulness.judge.json — these are the judge.create inputs. The instructions must reference at least one of {{ inputs }} / {{ outputs }} / {{ expectations }}. Click Continue plan; Aria merges and validates the inputs (a bad value is rejected and the form stays open), then — because autonomy is ask_each — raises an Aria needs your approval prompt. Click Approve to create the judge.
fill: Judges whether an assistant answer is faithful to its evidence.

You audit whether an assistant answer is faithful to its evidence. You are given the request {{ inputs }}, the model {{ outputs }}, and the reference {{ expectations }}.

Return true ONLY if every factual claim in {{ outputs }} is supported by {{ expectations }} (or by evidence cited in {{ inputs }}), and the answer makes no unsupported commitments. If any claim is unsupported, contradicted, or hallucinated, return false. Judge faithfulness only — not style.
steps.see: After Approve, judge.create shows DONE and the plan pauses on the review_queue.create form.

steps.where: Integrations and preview › Plans › PLAN-… (input form)
steps.do: Fill the review-queue form from governance-review.queue.json. The planner linked this step's name to the judge step's, so the form does not ask for a name — the queue will be created as AnswerFaithfulness. Enter the description and paste the four-question questions JSON array (the form rejects invalid JSON), click Continue plan, then Approve.
fill: Human spot-check of release-candidate answers: faithfulness, citation correctness, tone, and free-text notes. Pairs with the AnswerFaithfulness judge and the test set as the human layer of the governance kit.

[{"key": "faithful", "title": "Is the answer faithful to the evidence?", "type": "pass_fail", "required": true, "target": "feedback"}, {"key": "citation_ok", "title": "Are the citations correct and sufficient?", "type": "pass_fail", "required": false, "target": "feedback"}, {"key": "tone", "title": "Tone of the answer", "type": "categorical", "options": ["on_brand", "neutral", "off_brand"], "required": false, "target": "feedback"}, {"key": "notes", "title": "Reviewer notes", "type": "text", "required": false, "target": "feedback"}]
steps.see: After Approve, review_queue.create shows DONE and the plan moves on to eval_dataset.create.

steps.where: Integrations and preview › Plans › PLAN-… (interaction prompts)
steps.do: Finish the plan. eval_dataset.create has nothing to ask (its name is linked, so Aria creates an empty test set under the same name): click Approve. The last step, review_queue.add_items, shows a form for trace ids only (its queue_id is linked to the queue just created). There are no traces yet, so click Skip step.
steps.see: eval_dataset.create shows DONE, review_queue.add_items shows SKIPPED, and the plan reaches COMPLETED.
steps.asset: Plan completed (3 creates done, add_items skipped)

steps.where: Also in the alpha › Judges  +  Core journey › Test Sets  +  Operate › Review Queues
steps.do: Confirm the whole governance kit exists — three real artifacts from one sentence. Check each surface: Judges shows AnswerFaithfulness active; Test Sets shows an empty AnswerFaithfulness test set; Review Queues shows an AnswerFaithfulness queue with its four-question schema. Re-open the plan under Plans to see it COMPLETED with three steps done and review_queue.add_items skipped. (For differently named artifacts, create them on those pages from the specs in assets/.)
steps.see: An active judge AnswerFaithfulness, a test set and a review queue (both created under the judge's name) — the complete kit, built by the Aria plan.

steps.do: (Optional follow-up) Make the kit runnable end-to-end. Add example rows to the new test set (author them at /eval-datasets/:id → + Add example, or reuse the rows in 01-prompt-regression-lab/assets/dataset), then go to Core journey › Evaluations and run the dataset with the deterministic graders plus AnswerFaithfulness ticked under Custom LLM judges (it runs as a Judge.<id> scorer). Route any hard/low-confidence traces into the review queue via its Add traces to review box → Enqueue. Evaluations needs a real model provider — the default evaluator and LLM are fake, and Run evaluation returns a 400 without one.
steps.see: A scored evaluation run plus, optionally, traces enqueued into the review queue for human spot-checking — closing the eval + governance loop.
